headline: UCLA's passing game breaks Oregon's defensive will in road victory
body: UCLA's offense operated with surgical precision in the second half, exploiting Oregon's depleted secondary with a balanced attack that Oregon's defensive front simply could not disrupt. The Bruins moved the ball 392 yards with minimal resistance, and while the final margin of ten points suggests a competitive game, the gap in execution was wider than the scoreboard indicated. Nico Iamaleava threaded passes into tight windows all afternoon, completing 19 of 29 attempts for 270 yards and a touchdown, and his poise under pressure—Oregon never generated consistent heat—allowed UCLA's receivers to work in rhythm downfield.

Oregon's offensive identity crumbled against UCLA's pass rush. Thomas finished 11 of 27 for just 121 yards, a cautionary tale of what happens when a quarterback must hold the ball longer while receivers struggle to separate. Hughes provided the only genuine spark, grinding out 77 yards on 12 carries and punching in a touchdown, but one dimension could not sustain an entire offense. The Ducks' coaching staff will recognize that settling into a run-heavy approach after falling behind proved too passive; UCLA's defense tightened coverage and dared Thomas to beat them downfield, and he could not meet the challenge.

What began as a grinding, field-position game tilted decisively toward UCLA when the Bruins' secondary and pass rush synchronized in the third quarter, forcing Oregon into three straight three-and-outs. Those possessions represented the turning point—momentum never returned to Eugene. UCLA's defense, anchored by Pleasant's four tackles and a sack, suffocated Oregon's rhythm and allowed the Bruins' offense to dictate tempo. This was a game decided not by explosive plays but by control, and UCLA's coaching room imposed it from start to finish.
turningPoint: Oregon's three consecutive three-and-outs in the third quarter, triggered by UCLA's coordinated pass rush and coverage adjustments, allowed the Bruins to build an insurmountable lead while the Ducks' offense never found rhythm.

unsungHero.name: Pleasant
unsungHero.why: Four tackles and a sack from the defensive line may not generate the same attention as Iamaleava's passing performance, but shutting down Thomas's pocket and forcing Oregon into hurried decisions was every bit as crucial to the outcome as any touchdown pass.
